question:
QUESTION FROM THE OWNER, NOT A TRADING TURN (nothing changes in your books; not published). A quick naming vote.

One of the ten races is called "Currencies" on papertrades.ai (tabs, scoreboard, Telegram, Instagram, Discord). In it each AI trades currency pairs with leverage (long or short the yen, euro, US dollar, NZ dollar and so on), shown "like a forex account". The site is written for a general audience, and Beginner mode explains terms in plain words.

The owner asks: should the race be renamed "Forex" instead of "Currencies"? Options:
A) Keep "Currencies"
B) Rename to "Forex"
C) Something else (say what, e.g. "Forex (currencies)")

Consider: what newcomers understand at a glance, what traders search for and recognise, length in tabs and on small phone screens, and consistency with the other race names (Stocks and anything, Crypto, China stocks, Metals, Oil and energy, Options, Play it safe, Sports, Prediction markets). Answer in 3 to 5 sentences and start with your vote: "A", "B" or "C".

chatgpt.answer: B — Rename to “Forex”. It is shorter for tabs and phone screens, and it is the word traders search for and instantly recognise. “Currencies” is clearer for total beginners, but Beginner mode can explain it as “trading currency pairs like EUR/USD or USD/JPY.” If needed, use “Forex” as the race name and “currency pairs” as the subtitle or tooltip.

gemini.answer:
A. 

Keeping "Currencies" best serves your general audience because absolute beginners instantly understand it, whereas "Forex" can sound like intimidating jargon to outsiders. It is highly consistent with your other plain-English categories like "Metals" and "Crypto," favoring everyday language over industry terms. While "Forex" is shorter for small screens and instantly recognizable to veteran traders, "Currencies" still fits well in UI tabs and effectively bridges the gap for all skill levels. Ultimately, an experienced trader perfectly understands "Currencies," but a newcomer might not know what "Forex" means.
